Samples come in 8 'patient' groups; 'patient' explains 77% of the variance of the top expression components; neighbouring samples are spatially correlated (median Moran's I 0.14). Samples within a group are not independent, so whole groups are held out: grouped 4-fold cross-validation, each group tested exactly once, with one further group per fold held out for validation (early stopping and model selection).

The objective needs a shared space (joint_embedding, retrieval, cross_modal_prediction) and there are about 8,511 training pairs. Contrastive alignment learns that space directly from the pairing: each sample's partner is its positive and the other samples in the batch its negatives (InfoNCE, a lower bound on the mutual information between modalities).
Highest screening score among 4 candidates (alignment_recall_at_10 0.087 on held-out screening samples). Screened on 2000 training and 500 validation samples from separate groups.
Each patch covers the spot's own footprint (145 px), the tissue its RNA was captured from; resized to the encoder's input size.
28% of the variance in mean image colour lies between groups (ICC >= 20%); a frozen encoder would encode stain/scanner differences as signal. Colour statistics are matched to the training data.
'expression' is a matrix modality; no pretrained encoder applies, so a small MLP is trained on the preprocessed features.

chosen: library-size normalisation to the median library size, then log1p; top 2,000 variable; pca
rationale: genes matrix, 83% zeros, median library 3,231 (integer counts): library-size normalisation to the median library size, then log1p; keep the 2,000 most variable features (fitted on training folds only); then PCA to 100 components (fitted on training data): about 8,511 training samples for 2,000 features is < 5 per feature, so compressing first reduces parameters and count noise.

About 8,511 training pairs: a 256-d joint space with 2-layer heads (512 hidden) is small relative to n; batch 512 gives 511 negatives per positive; early stopping on validation (patience 15) and a 180s cap per fit; temperature learned from 0.07.

Frozen pretrained backbones with small trainable projection heads: few trainable parameters for the number of pairs (low variance), features computed once. Fine-tuning not tried: no pre-aligned dual encoder among the chosen encoders.

chosen: dropout 0.2 (was 0.1), weight_decay 1e-3 (was 1e-4), in all three configs
rationale: Patient explains 77% of the variance of the top expression components (group_silhouette 0.63). With 8 patients and grouped 4-fold CV plus one validation patient, each fit trains on only about 5 patients. The heads can therefore memorise patient-specific expression offsets that will not carry over to the held-out patients. Somewhat stronger regularisation, together with early stopping on a held-out patient, guards against this. Applying the same change to every config keeps the comparisons controlled.

phikon is best on all three screening metrics: alignment recall@10 0.087 vs ≤0.063, ridge R² 0.215 vs ≤0.184, and probe macro-F1 0.43 vs ≤0.39. Its pretraining corpus is TCGA histology tiles, which include stained tissue of possibly similar type. It has no zero-shot partner, so no zero-shot score is inflated. Some overlap in tissue domain may still favour it in the frozen-feature baselines, so this should be noted when reporting. Fine-tuning is not used: 4 folds x 1200 s would exceed the 2700 s total budget.

The primary's mean validation R@10 is 0.0335. That is about 6x chance (≈0.0054) and beats CCA in all 4 folds (0.0179; +0.016 ± 0.009). So the alignment is real but weak, which is expected when held-out patients contain many spots that look nearly identical. For prediction from histology the primary is tied with ridge (Pearson top-50: 0.148 vs 0.152; better in 2/4 folds). For clustering it is tied with the unimodal and CCA baselines. However, the hard_infonce comparison beats the primary on R@10 in every fold (0.0539/0.0211/0.0347/0.0510 vs 0.0492/0.0148/0.0319/0.0382). Its mean is 0.040 vs 0.034, with paired differences of +0.0028 to +0.0128 (mean +0.0066, SD ≈0.0044). The automated flag calls the hard_infonce gap 'within noise', but the paired, per-fold comparison is consistent. Every fold improves: a paired t of about 3.0 with 3 degrees of freedom, and a sign test of 4/4. That is moderate evidence, not conclusive. There is also a plausible reason for the gain. Soft InfoNCE spreads target probability across spots with similar expression (23% are near-twins). That rewards retrieving look-alikes instead of the exact paired spot, and exact pairing is what R@10 measures. Hard InfoNCE also leaves the regression term and every other setting unchanged, so it should not cost anything on prediction. Its training curves overfit faster: train loss falls to about 2.0 while validation loss stays around 8–9, and folds 2 and 3 peak early (epochs 7 and 3). Early stopping on the retrieval score already handles this, and the selected checkpoints still beat the primary's. Switching needs no extra compute and carries no risk of a regression.
